WIDNES POLICE COURT. Mom:ay.—Before Messrs. F. H. Gossage (chairman) and Holb rook Gaskell, jun. VIOLENT CONDUCT IN AN EATING•HOUSE.—Bridget Weir was charged with having broken a window in Mrs. Uns- worth's eating-house, Victoria-road, and also with being drunk and disorderly.—Mrs. TJnsworth said the prisoner entered the house and behaved in such a disorderly manner that she asked her to leave, but she refused. Prisoner retaliated by breaking a large window, and she gave her into the custody of P.C. Murray.—Weir, who, it appeared from the statement of the Inspector, had been up before, was ordered to pay 255. 6d. with costs, and including Bs. 6d., the value of the broken pane. In default, she was sentenced to 14 days' imprisonment. A LOAFER ASSAULTING A POLICE OFFICER. John Hannon was charged with having been drunk and disorderly and assaulting P.C. Pitt.—The officer said that about quarter to eleven on Saturday night he saw the prisoner standing in Waterloo-road, at a corner of the street, with several other loafers. He was drunk mid causing an ob- struction, and he therefore asked him to move on, and advised him to do so quietly'. Prisoner then struck him a blow on the eye and behaved in a very violent manner. A large crowd assembled and a general uproar took place in I the street.—The Inspector said that this was the 18th appearance of the prisoner, who, in 1870, suffered two months' imprisonment for assaulting a police officer. He would withdraw the charge of drunkenness against him.— Hannon was sentenced to three months' imprisonment with hard labour. DRUNK ON LICENSED PREMISES. Thomas Walsh was convicted, on the evidence of P.C. Laing, of having been drunk at the Waterloo Vaults Waterloo-road, on Saturday night and refused to leave. He was fined 2s. 6d. and costs. A LEGAL POlNT.—Michael McGuinn was charged with having been drunk in Waterloo-road, and broken a-window at the shop of Mr. Edward Johnson, grocer. Evidence was given by the Inspector of police, P.C. Skinner, and Mr. Peter Monoghan, assistant to Mr. Johnson. It appeared that this was the prisoner's eighth appearance in court. On Saturday night, about a quarter to nine, whilst drunk, he fell through one of the large windows in the shop. Mr. Lewin, Deputy Magistrates' Clerk, said that as the prisoner did not do the damage wilfully, Mr. Johnson would have to sue him in the County Court to recover the amount owing.—Prisoner was fined 10s. and costs on the first charge, with the alternative of 14 days' imprisonment. The second charge was dismissed. THE RESULT OF TRYING TO RESCUE His WIFE.—MArtiII Weir was charged with attempting to rescue his wife Bridget from P.C. Murray, as he was taking her to the police station. The officer gave evidence as to Weir seizing him by the arm, and trying to release the woman. As the prisoner was stated to be an old offender, he was lined 40s. and costs, and, in default of payment, ordered to be sent to gaol two months, with hard labour. WEDNESDAY—Before Messrs. Holbrook Gaskell, sen. (chair- man), H. S. Hall, George Pilkington, F. H. Gossage, and Holbrook Gaskell, jun. APPLICATION FOR A THEATRICAL LICENSE.—Mr. Lewin, deputy magistrates' clerk, addressing the Bench, said that was a special sessions, held for the purpose of hearing an application for a theatrical license from M. Joseph Fields. The applicant had given notice on the matter, and their worships were present in response. However, on Monday Mr. Fields wrote a letter stating that he would not be able to attend in consequence of ill-health. He had sent him a communication in reply stating that if possible he must be present to make the application in person, but he had not then arrived. He understood that for some time Mr. Fields had been manager and proprietor of the Gaiety Theatre, Winsford.—ln answer to the Chairman, Superintendent Barker said the proper course in the matter would have been for the applicant to have communicated with him, so that he might have written the chief of police at Winsford, and handed in a report as to the gentleman's character, but he had not done so.—Mr. Lewin, in answer to a question from one of the Bench, said Mr. Fields had written requesting that the special sessions might be adjourned, but, of course, as it was a sessions called for a special purpose, it was not possible to adjourn it. He understood that the license was required for a building which was to be put upon the market ground, and the request was that the license might extend over a period of twelve months. Mr. Fields would have to pay rent to the local authority.—The Chairman asked if , there was any gentleman present representing the Local Board.—Mr. Lewin believed there was not. The applicant would simply rent the ground from the Local Board. He had observed circuses and other kinds of entertainments on the fair ground.—Mr. Hall said there was a difference in this particular case, as it was proposed to license the building.— The Chairman remarked that it appeared the Superintendent of Police knew nothing about the application and nothing about the applicant. He (the speaker) quite coincided with an obser- vation which had fallen from Mr. Hall, to the effect that the magistrates would be quite ready to grant a theatrical license to any person who gave them reason to believe that the place to be occupied would be properly conducted.— After a brief consultation, the magistrates decided to adjourn the consideration of the application until the following Wednesday, in order that the police might make enquiries in reference to the applicant. —The Chairman said the magistrates would grant a license upon the police being satisfied that the building would be properly conducted. Before Mr. George Pilkington. ANNOYING A. NEIGHBOURHOOD.—Mary Daly was sum- moned for causing a breach of the peace on the 15t1.i inst. Defendant was amusing herself by cursing, swearing, and causing a terrible disturbance in Oxford-street, at twelve o'clock at night. —Defendant said that she was very much excited at the time, and she hoped the Bench would look leniently upon her offence.—Mr. Pilkington remarked that the summons would be dismissed on defendant paving 7s. 6d. costs, which she agreed to do. MERSEY MISSIONS TO SEAMEN (RUNCORN BRANCH.)—It has been decided to build or purchase a House for the Missionary connected with the above branch, Donations in aid of the same will be thankfully received by the Treasurer, E. A. Ohorlton, Esq. Parr's Banking Company, Runcorn. It has also been decided to hold a CHRISTMAS TREE andSALE OF WORK on TRUrSDAY and FRIDAY, DECEMBER 29th and 30th, 1881, in the Puntac HALL RUNCORN. The follow- ing ladies have kindly consented to preside at the stalls and to receive all parcels or donations towards the same :—Mrs. Lloyd Wigg, Mrs. Dr. Steele, Miss Barclay, Miss Williams, Percival's- lane ; Miss Mourita, High-street; Miss Norman, Greenway- road ; Miss Garratt, Albert-street; Miss S. E. Statham, Trenth- am-street; Misses Owen, Brackley-street ; Miss Ooleburd, Church-street. Miss Davies. Brackiey-street ; Mrs. E Bellings-. ley, Astridge-street ; Mrs. Oroley, Bridge-street; Mrs. Bankes, Weston ; Miss Clarke, Weaver Villa, Weston Point; Mr. Shaw, Missionary; or any of the Sunday School Teachers. Weekly Sewing Meetings will be held at the Mission-room, Bottom Locks, every Wednesday from 2to 9 p.m. Tea will be pro- vided at 6 o'clock. Workers, 6d. each; visitors, Is. All interested in the work will have la hearty welcome.

ST. AMBROSE CHURCH, WIDNES. A GRAND BAZAAR Will be held in the VOLUNTEER HALL, WIDNES, On WEDNESDAY. THURSDAY, and FRIDAY, the 9th, 10th, and 11th of NOVEMBER, 1881, To raise a sufficient sum of money to pay off a small balance due to the Building Committe, but chieMy to provide a Fund for the Endowment and Consecration of the Church. The Bazaar will be OPENED on WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 9th, at 1 o'clock, by CLARKE ASPINALL, ESQ., J.P., (of Liverpool.) J. BROCK, FSQ., J.P., H. BRUNNER, ESQ., E. CAREY, ESQ., H. WADE DEACON, ESQ., REV. G. HOILOWAY, (Vicar of Earn- worth), REV. B. A. SPOONER. Curate-in charge of St. Ambrose. There will be a REFRESHMENT STALL; and on the opening day Luncheon will be provided at 1-30 p.m., tickets 2s. 6d. each. The Hall will be Aecorated in representation on an OLD ENGLISH MARKET PLACE OF THE lku CENTURY, in the centre of which wid be erected a full sized model of an ancient Itarket,Cross. During each day at intervals selections of Vocal and Instrum- ental MUSIC will be given. PROFESSOR WEBER,the eminent Conjurer and Ventriloquist, will also give a series of Perfor- mances at frequent intervals during each day. The programme will also include other amusements and ex- hibitions, of which due notice will be given. Admissi.n Season Tickets, 2e. each (not transferable); Wednesday up to 6 o'clock, Is. 61., after 6, is.; Thursday (all day), Is.; Friday (all day), 6d. WARRINGTON GRAMMAR SCHOOL. PRE B SCHOLARSHIPS. An EXAMINATION, to elect four free scholars, will be held at the GRAMMAR SCHOOL, at 10 a.m., on FRIDAY, DEC. 16th, 1881. Candidates must be under 12 years of age on beptamber 30th, 1881. These scholarships are open only to boys who nave been for three years under instruction at some public elemen- tary school within the school district of Warrington. All applications for admission to the Examination must be sent in before Thursday, December Ist; and must be accom- panied with certificates of age, of character, and of three years, attendance at a public elementary school. For further par. ticulas apply to tho READ MASTER.

WIDNES SCIENCE AND ART CLASSES.— In connection with the Science and Art Department, Kensington, and City and Guilds of London Institute. —Session 1881-82.—The eighth Session has now commenced. SYLLABUS : Mondays : Inorganic Chemistry. 6-30 to 8-0 p.m.; Alkali Manufacture, 8-0 to 9-0 p.m. Tuesdays: Art —Freehand Drawing, 6-30 to 8-0 p In.; Machine Construction and Drawing, 8-0 to 9-0 p.m. Wednesdays: Art—Freehand Drawing, 6-30 to 8-0 p.m.; Building Construction and Draw- ing, 8-0 to 9-0 p.m. Fridays: Sound, Light? and Heat, 7-0 to 8-0 p.m.; Mathematics, 8-0 to 9-0 p Tn. The Technologi- cal Class (Alkali Manufacture) will include the manufacture of Sulphuric Acid, Sulphate of Soda, Soda Ash, Caustic Soda, Soda Crystals, and Blesching Powder. Candidates eligible for the Technological Class (Alkali Manufacture) must be actually employed in Chemical or other allied works, and they must have passed, or pass during the coming session, in two of the following-named subjects :—Machine Construction, Building Construction, Theoretical Mechanics, Applied Mechanics, Acoustics, Light and Heat And Inorganic Chemistry.:- Fee, 3s. per class, payable in advance. No class will commenee unless a sufficient number of students join. Those who intend to join' these classes must do so before the end of October. JOSEPH 3IORBISON, Hon. Sec. nOROUGH OF ST. HELENS. TO THE BURGESSES OF ECCLESTON WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,—I beg to thank you for the honour yen have done me by returning me again, unopposed, as one of your representatives in the Town Council. I would assure you that it will ever be my study and desire to secure the interests of your Ward, and of the Borough at large. I remain, Ladies and Gentlemen. Your faithful servant, RICHARD EILKINGTON. Class Works, 24th October, 1881.

BOROUGH OF ST. HELENS. TO THE BURGESSES OF PARR WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,—I beg to tender you my warmest thanks for again returning me as one of the representatives of this Ward. I will endeavour, to the best of my abilities, to study the interests of this Ward and the Borough in general, so as to merit the confidence you have again placed in me. Yours faithfully, THOMAS WALKER. Merton Bank Alkali Works, 24th October, 1881.
